Keene.housing_era: A small city with a classic brick Main Street, 19th-century and early-1900s homes, Keene State College-area housing, post-war neighborhoods, and rural edges under the Monadnock foothills.

Keene.wildlife_intro:
Keene's older homes and college-area rentals produce steady bat, raccoon and gray squirrel calls, with mice moving through multifamily housing and skunks denning under porches citywide. The Ashuelot River corridor brings raccoons and beavers into low neighborhoods, and the wooded edges add woodchucks, fishers and porcupines around outbuildings. Bat colonies in Keene's 19th-century attics are a defining summer issue.

Our crew schedules Keene bat exclusion outside the May 15 to August 15 restriction, inspecting through summer and sealing in fall. Fall also brings student-rental calls and the shelter-seeking rush before the Monadnock-region winter. Spring opens with woodchucks under sheds and raccoon families in chimneys. Most Keene jobs pair removal with a full sealing pass on older construction, where entries are rarely single.

faqs.q: How much does wildlife removal cost in Keene, NH?
faqs.a: Cost depends on the animal, how it got in, and how much sealing or cleanup the home needs, so our crew inspects first and explains the options before any work starts.  Simple single-entry squirrel jobs cost less than full attic exclusion or bat work, and we never quote a firm figure before seeing the structure.

faqs.q: Are porcupines a problem in Keene, or only out in the country?
faqs.a: Both. Wooded Keene lots and even in-town outbuildings get porcupine chewing, especially on plywood, deck boards and salted wood in late winter. City dogs are the usual victims when a porcupine settles under a shed. Our crew can remove a resident animal and advise on screening the den space.

Swanzey.wildlife_intro:
Swanzey's villages and farm country sit under Mount Monadnock, and wildlife pressure is steady. Raccoons and gray squirrels get into farmhouse and village attics, bats roost in older homes and barns, and skunks and woodchucks work yards and field edges. Porcupines are a real Swanzey nuisance, chewing outbuildings, decks and plywood, and fishers move through the Ashuelot corridor and deep woods, occasionally hitting chicken coops.

Winters are long and cold here, so fall sealing matters — our crew checks chimneys, soffits and barn openings before animals settle in. Spring brings woodchuck and raccoon denning, and summer bat colonies are inspected for exclusion after August 15. Swanzey jobs often cover a house and its outbuildings together, since a determined animal denied one building simply tries the next.

faqs.q: How much does wildlife removal cost in Swanzey, NH?
faqs.a: Cost depends on the animal, how it got in, and how much sealing or cleanup the home needs, so our crew inspects first and explains the options before any work starts. faqs.q: A fisher killed our Swanzey chickens. How do we protect the next flock?
faqs.a: Fishers slip through surprisingly small gaps and climb well, so coops need hardware cloth — not chicken wire — over every opening, a secure door latch, and birds locked in at night. Our crew can check the coop after an attack, remove a fisher that has settled nearby, and point out the weak spots to fix.

Thorndike Pond camps open in spring to mice and bat evidence, and the Contoocook headwaters keep beavers and raccoons moving through low ground.

Seasonal pond properties drive a lot of our Jaffrey work — spring openings, fall closings, and sealing in between so animals do not overwinter inside. Year-round homes follow the usual rhythm: spring litters, summer bat inspections with exclusion after August 15, and heavy fall shelter-seeking. Jaffrey's cold winters reward homes that get sealed early, before snow makes roof work slow and difficult.

Woodchucks dig along field edges and under outbuildings, skunks den under porches, and beavers dam Cold River tributaries, flooding low fields and roads.

Spring in Walpole means woodchucks out, raccoons denning in barns, and bats returning — with exclusion planned for after August 15. Fall brings the sealing season before the valley winter. Our crew often works whole farmsteads here, checking feed storage, barn gaps and the house together, because river-valley farms give animals food, water and shelter all in one place.

faqs.q: Are red squirrels really worse than gray squirrels in Rindge attics?
